reading.title: Evening on the Porch
reading.purpose: Spend an evening with a park ranger and a child who learn how animals find food and stay safe.
paras: Lena and her uncle Samir sat on the porch at the edge of the woods, waiting for the sun to set. Uncle Samir was a park ranger, and he knew the sounds of every animal.

A squirrel hurried past, hunting for acorns. "She will forage until dark," whispered Samir. Then a raccoon waddled out and tipped over a trash can. "He will scavenge anything that people leave behind," said Samir.
A gray moth landed on the tree trunk and seemed to vanish. Lena leaned closer. The moth's wings matched the bark so well that she could not see it until it moved. "That is camouflage," said Samir.

Far overhead, geese called as they flew south. "They migrate every fall," said Samir. "Nobody taught them. They follow instinct, a way of acting they are born knowing." Just then a cat began to prowl along the fence, moving low and quiet. The squirrel fled up the nearest tree, running away fast.

Before bed, Samir told Lena about a small bird that is endangered, because only a few are left. "New roads and loud noise threaten its nest," he said. Lena promised to tell her class how to protect it.

choices: a skill that young animals learn from older teachers
a long trip taken only during the summer months
a way of acting that an animal is born knowing
a fear of loud sounds and bright lights at night
qs.why: The sentence explains it: instinct is "a way of acting they are born knowing," and nobody taught the geese.

qs.q: Which sentence tells how the moth hid on the tree?
choices: A gray moth landed on the tree trunk and seemed to vanish.
Far overhead, geese called as they flew south.
The moth's wings matched the bark so well that she could not see it until it moved.
qs.why: This sentence says why the moth could not be seen: its wings matched the bark.

ev.text: The moth's wings matched the bark so well that she could not see it until it moved.

qs.q: Why did the squirrel flee up the tree?
choices: It sensed danger from the cat nearby.
It wanted to follow the geese flying south for the winter.
It was hunting for acorns that were higher up in the branches.
It heard Samir whisper and felt scared of the porch.
qs.why: A cat began to prowl along the fence just before the squirrel ran, so the squirrel fled from danger.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this story?
choices: Animals are only active at night, so people should always keep out of the woods.
Animals have many ways to find food and stay safe, and some need help.
Uncle Samir wants Lena to become a park ranger when she grows up.
Raccoons and cats are the biggest danger to every small bird in the woods.
qs.why: Each paragraph shows an animal finding food, hiding, or running from danger, and the last one is about helping an endangered bird.

clues.text: a way of acting they are born knowing
because only a few are left
